body:
Closes #10

Ticket: [ALBUM-10](https://github.com/dbeallor/album-ranker/issues/10)
Spec: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-21-album-10-spreadsheet-import.md`
As-built: `docs/superpowers/as-built/2026-11-21-album-10-spreadsheet-import.md`

## What this does

- `npm run import -- "<path>"` reads the Albums sheet, matches each row to a MusicBrainz album, and writes year entries and decade list entries.
- Rows it can't match with confidence (typo, tie, album already placed, rank already used) go to a review page at `/import`, where the user picks a match, keeps a manual album, moves an album, or skips.
- Exact duplicates merge; re-running is safe; a summary names merged duplicates and conflicting placements.
- Migration `002_import.sql` adds `source_decade_rank` and review reason columns. Catalog results gain the artist's MusicBrainz id. New dependencies: `read-excel-file`, `write-excel-file` (dev, fixture only).

Context size: pass skipped (not collective-wisdom)

## Proof

- **Typo row lands on the review page, not the data**: `lib/import/run.test.ts` ("sends the typo, ambiguous, duplicate and repeated-rank rows to review with reasons") and `lib/import/write-row.test.ts`, on a fixture of made-up rows.
- **A second import changes nothing**: `lib/import/run.test.ts` re-run test (second run reports `alreadyImported`, no new rows, a skipped review item stays skipped).
- **Tests use a fixture covering each row kind, a duplicate and a rank-plus-honorable-mention row**: `lib/import/fixtures/albums.xlsx` (made-up rows, generated by `npm run import:fixture`).
- **Decade lists follow the sheet's ranks even when rows resolve out of order**: `lib/db/decade-lists.test.ts` and `lib/import/resolve.test.ts`.

  ```
  $ npm test
  Test Files  24 passed (24)
        Tests  317 passed (317)
  $ npm run lint && npm run typecheck && npm run build   # all clean
  ```

Not proven:
- Importing the user's real `Best Albums.xlsx` end to end and the 1960s, 2000s and 2010s decade lists matching the sheet: the file is personal and not in the repo, the run takes about 15 minutes against live MusicBrainz, and no year pages exist yet (#6). Tests use made-up rows and a fake catalog.
- The script against live MusicBrainz: never run against it; tests use a fake catalog.
- The review page in a browser: covered by component tests only, no screenshot.

---

feat: ALBUM-10 import columns and decade insert by source rank

commits.messageBody:
Add .ts extensions to the db modules' relative imports and declare
CatalogError.kind as a field, so Node's type stripping can load them
(the import script runs as node scripts/import.ts). Add
findYearEntryBySource, setSourceDecadeRank and getImportReviewItem, and
an optional artistId on CatalogCandidate so a saved candidate keeps its
artist.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
commits.messageHeadline: feat: ALBUM-10 db and catalog helpers for the import script

commits.messageBody:
read-excel-file reads .xlsx only (no write path, so nothing to misuse on
the user's file), is actively maintained (9.3.20, published this week),
has a small dependency set (fflate, saxen) and works on Node 24+ in the
node entry point. It returns cell values, not formulas, which is what the
import wants. Alternatives rejected: SheetJS on npm is stale and
unmaintained there, exceljs is far larger and write-capable.

write-excel-file (devDependency, same author) generates the committed
fixture lib/import/fixtures/albums.xlsx from made-up rows with
npm run import:fixture. The import and import:fixture npm scripts are
added here.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
commits.messageHeadline: feat: ALBUM-10 xlsx reader dependency and fixture spreadsheet

commits.messageBody:
Reads the Albums sheet by header (input Rank right of Album), validates
rows, merges case-insensitive duplicates, and picks a catalog match by
normalized title and artist with the catalog search injected.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
commits.messageHeadline: feat: ALBUM-10 sheet reading, row mapping, normalizing and matching

commits.messageBody:
Each row is written in its own transaction (album, shared artist, year
entry with source key and decade rank, decade insert, or a review item
with reason). The run skips rows already imported, retries catalog
failures at 5 and 15 seconds, stops after ten failed rows in a row, and
formats the summary.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
commits.messageHeadline: feat: ALBUM-10 per-row write, run loop and summary

commits.messageBody:
npm run import -- "<path>" reads the file before opening the database,
throttles MusicBrainz to the existing 1.1 s spacing and prints progress
every 25 rows. It runs under node --conditions=react-server so the
server-only marker resolves to its empty module outside Next.js.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

resolveReviewItem creates or reuses the album, adds the year and decade
entries (or moves an existing year entry here) and resolves the item in
one transaction; a taken rank fails naming the holder and leaves the item
open. skipReviewItem marks an item skipped.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
